question: How do I choose k for k-means?
reference_answer: Plot inertia for a range of k and look for the elbow.

evidence.title: Choosing k: the elbow method
evidence.slide_text: Run k-means for k = 1 to 10. Record inertia (within-cluster sum of squares). Plot inertia against k. Pick k where the curve bends: the elbow.
evidence.speaker_notes: Inertia always falls as k grows, so do not pick the minimum. Look for diminishing returns.

segments.narration: On this slide we run k-means for k from one to ten and record the inertia each time, which is the within-cluster sum of squares. Then we plot inertia against k. Inertia always falls as k grows, so the smallest value is not the answer. Look for the elbow, where the curve bends and adding more clusters gives diminishing returns.

about: Narration adds a rule and a number that are not on the slide
question: How do I choose k for k-means?

evidence.title: Choosing k: the elbow method
evidence.slide_text: Run k-means for k = 1 to 10. Record inertia. Plot inertia against k. Pick k where the curve bends: the elbow.

segments.narration: On this slide you can see the rule of thumb: k should always be the square root of half your number of rows, which works 95 percent of the time according to a 2019 Stanford study. If your data has 200 rows, use k of 10 and you are done, no plotting needed.
